client.business_description: A neighborhood specialty coffee shop and bakery focused on locally roasted beans, fresh pastries, and a cozy place to gather.
client.avoid: Nothing corporate, cold, or high-tech feeling
client.content_owner: Designer writes the copy from the owner's notes
client.media_owner: Owner shares phone photos; designer may source a few stock images

sections.notes: Simple warm nav, logo centered or left, a 'Visit Us' link that stands out.
Cozy photo of the space or a latte on the right. Headline should feel personal and inviting.
Owner's story — why the cafe exists. A candid photo beats a polished one here.
Pastries, drinks, and the room. Warmth sells the visit — show the atmosphere.
Terracotta band: 'Come say hi' with hours and a Get Directions button.
Hours, address, and a small message form. Keep it relaxed, not formal.
Hours, social links, and location. Friendly sign-off line.
Use the pricing layout as a menu board: Coffee, Tea, Bakery columns with item rows and prices.
A few hero shots of signature items.

reference_insights: Let warm photography of the space and the food lead — the site should feel like a personal invitation to drop by, not a transaction.

reference_details.nav_pattern: Lightweight top nav with a clear 'Visit Us' link; warm, uncluttered.
reference_details.hero_pattern: Split hero with an inviting lifestyle photo and a short, personal headline.
reference_details.content_pattern: Story-first sections with generous photography and plenty of breathing room.
reference_details.cta_pattern: Gentle, recurring 'Come visit' prompts with hours and directions rather than hard sells.
trust_elements: lots of real photos of the space
reference_details.what_to_borrow: The photo-led, story-first feel that makes a visitor want to come in and sit down.
reference_details.what_to_avoid: Avoid dense menus or anything that feels corporate or high-tech — it would break the cozy mood.

constraints: Keep everything warm and hand-crafted. Avoid cold, corporate, or high-tech styling; favor soft edges, natural tones, and friendly type.
designer_summary: Bloom Cafe wants to feel like a warm neighborhood favorite — cozy, personal, and photo-led. Use a soft terracotta-and-sage palette with friendly type, and let the owner's real photos carry the mood. Watch-out: keep CTAs gentle and avoid anything that reads as corporate or transactional.
palette_rationale: A warm terracotta primary feels inviting and hand-crafted, balanced by a soft sage accent and a creamy background that together evoke a cozy, natural cafe atmosphere.
font_rationale: Lora brings a gentle, friendly warmth to headings, paired with the rounded, highly readable Nunito for an approachable body voice.
